groups.title: Testing philosophy: unit, integration, and end-to-end
groups.question: Your MERN app has no tests yet, and you want confidence before each deploy without a slow, flaky suite. Explain which kinds of tests you'd write, how many of each, and what you'd fake in them.

followUps.The testing pyramid and where to invest: Why have many unit tests, fewer integration tests and only a few end-to-end tests?
followUps.What to mock and what not to mock in uni: What should you mock in a unit test, and what goes wrong if you mock too much?

evidence.text: Unit tests check small pieces alone, integration tests check pieces together with real dependencies like the database, and end-to-end tests drive the real app in a browser.
Lower levels are fast and cheap, while higher levels give more confidence but are slower and flakier, so there are fewer of them.

notEnough: Only naming unit, integration and end-to-end tests without explaining the trade-off.

evidence.text: Unit tests mock external dependencies like HTTP calls and databases, so they're fast and only test your logic.
Those dependencies are tested for real in integration tests.
Mocking too much makes tests pass even when the real pieces don't work together.

notEnough: Only saying mock dependencies without saying which ones or why.

groups.title: React Testing Library's guiding principle
groups.question: You're testing a React login form with React Testing Library. Explain how your tests should find the email field and the submit button, and why.

followUps.Query hierarchy: getByRole first, test I: Why prefer getByRole over a test id, and what does that give you for free?

evidence.text: Queries mirror how users find things: by role, label or text first, with test ids as a last resort.
getByRole only finds elements with the right accessible role and name, so it also catches accessibility problems.
Tests tied to what users see don't break when the internal markup changes.

notEnough: Only saying use getByRole without explaining why it's preferred.

groups.title: Writing Jest unit and integration tests
groups.question: You need tests for a price calculation helper, and for the POST /api/posts endpoint of your Express app, which requires auth. Explain how you'd write both with Jest.

followUps.describe/it blocks, beforeEach setup, an: How would you organize the helper's tests, and what do beforeEach and matchers like toEqual and toThrow do?
followUps.Supertest for testing Express endpoints: How does Supertest call your Express app without starting a server, and what would you check for POST /api/posts?

evidence.text: describe groups related tests and it or test defines each case.
beforeEach runs setup before every test, so each one starts from a clean state.
Matchers check results, for example toEqual for deep equality, toThrow for errors and toHaveBeenCalledWith for mocks.

notEnough: Only listing Jest functions without saying what they do.

misconceptions.text: Says toBe compares two objects by their contents.

evidence.text: Supertest takes the Express app and sends real HTTP requests to it inside the test process, without starting a server on a port.
The request goes through routing, middleware like auth and validation, and the handler.
The test checks status codes and response bodies, for example 401 without a token and 201 with valid input.

notEnough: Only saying use Supertest without saying what is checked.

groups.title: Async testing and CI integration
groups.question: Your React component loads data and shows it after a moment, and your tests sometimes fail randomly. You also want tests to run on every push. Explain how you'd test async UI reliably and set up the CI run.

followUps.Testing async components with waitFor an: Why use findBy queries or waitFor instead of waiting a fixed number of milliseconds?
followUps.Running jest with --coverage and integra: What does --coverage report, and how would a GitHub Actions workflow stop a broken pull request?

evidence.text: findBy queries return a promise that keeps retrying until the element appears or a timeout passes.
waitFor retries an assertion until it passes, for state that changes asynchronously.
Fixed waits are either too short, causing random failures, or too long, slowing the suite.

notEnough: Only saying await the test without explaining retrying queries.

evidence.text: jest --coverage reports which lines and branches the tests ran, showing untested code.
A GitHub Actions workflow runs the tests on every push or pull request.
A failing test, or coverage below a set threshold, fails the check so the pull request can't be merged.

notEnough: Only saying run tests in CI without explaining what makes it fail.

misconceptions.text: Says high test coverage proves the code is correct.
